title: Communication Strategies: Penetrate Their Minds
coreMove: Enter the audience's frame so communication answers their real decision instead of displaying your own intelligence.
sourcePressure: Communication can persuade respectfully or manipulate by bypassing reflection; the distinction must stay explicit.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Polish language until it sounds clever to the speaker but misses the receiver's filters.

sourceAnchors.name: Cicero and Lincoln
sourceAnchors.detail: the source says Strategy 30 draws on the rhetorical tradition, naming Cicero and Lincoln, and on modern advertising.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Cicero and Lincoln belong here because rhetoric is not ornament; it is the discipline of meeting an audience inside its judgment.

hook: Do not open with a battlefield metaphor for Communication Strategies: Penetrate Their Minds.
Do not start by saying strategy is not about violence.
counterintuition: Avoid the reusable correction frame that the move is not X but Y.
Avoid a bland paradox about strength looking like weakness.
tryThisNow: No generic timer, pause, breathe, or list-three-options prompt.
No reusable ask what matters most prompt.
examples: No generic founder in a pitch deck unless the domain requires it.
No battlefield reenactment or invented historical anecdote.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person 'You' direct address, retrospective 'It took her three weeks to see', question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
